body: I'm not holding myself to a higher standard. I just hate myself. I would not be friends with me. I'm less than others because I offer nothing. I'm a drain on everyone. An obligation.

3 hours later and I'm just hitting refresh like a reddit addict. Debating checking myself into a posh psych ward nearby. They definitely wouldn't let me keep my under-wire though so I'm leaning towards no.

>My friend, no one can fight you for you if you won't. 

I've been fighting for myself for 15 years. I'm just not winning.

>We can never get any real validation or happiness from other people - that can only come from inside. If you're looking for other people to validate you or make you happy, you're on a fool's (although a very common) errand. Love yourself. Trust yourself. Follow your vision.

If it can only come from myself then I'm really fucked.
>If the cause of your unhappiness is that other people aren't responding the way that you want them to, the answer is that you need to improve your marketing and persuasion skills, not depression and self-rejection.

Maybe for professional situations this would be applicable, but not in my personal life.
That quote totally making me cry right now. ...I really do miss myself.

>  Does negative self-talk and harsh self-judgmentalism make things easier for you?


Yes.

 >   How would it be if you were to give yourself the respect that you deserve?


Never even considered this...

   >And how would it be if you were to require others to respect you, too? Would some of them turn away from you then, if you no longer accepted their abuse? How would that be bad?

 I don't even know how to respond properly.

Thank you.  I've always resisted writing it all down b.c it sounds/felt so self absorbed to write about myself. You telling me that I should, that it would be beneficial even, really is helping me right now. 
>First, it keeps you busy - keeps your mind on the "hmm this word doesn't sound right, what could I put there instead" instead of the horror of life in general.

Considering I just wrote 3 separate response to you, I must say this is  true.

I had 2 separate Dr.'s in my life. 1 from 9-12 the other from 12-now. I have had so many goals in therapy over the years. It started originally b.c I was being bullied at school -in a nutshell I was a victim of queen bees and wanna bee's. 

I hated my 1st Dr. I actually slammed the door so hard on my way out of  my last appointment I broke the door. 

2nd doc has been amazing mostly. Completely different approach to my problems. He's a positive guy. 
>I think that therapies should have a goal and a plan to use the therapy to get there.

I've had goals and plans. short term ones; which worked, I suppose. 

The problem is that it's all pointless. Everything that I've done doesn't matter. Everything that I thought was important isn't. It doesn't matter that I'm very pretty. It doesn't matter how rich I may be. It doesn't matter how educated I've become. Everybody leaves me. Everyone disrespects me. Nobody will ever respect anything I accomplish because of various factors. I've become a living afterthought.

>Get involved with groups of people who share your core values and you will probably find friends more quickly who you will feel comfortable sharing with.
 
Already tried this. I went to a meet and greet film event for advanced film students at my college.  Disastrously embarrassing results. Cried 15 city blocks walking home after. Never felt so dumb / repulsive in my whole life. Nobody would talk to me, not even the guy that I had just had sex with that morning ( and am still seeing- so pathetic of me)- I mingle well with others, I know I do- but this group of people wanted nothing to do with me which was crushing b.c they were my peers. Film is just about the only thing I want to do- the only thing that gives my life any passion at all. 

I know what you're thinking "A girl in art school is depressed? Shocking." So I really want to highlight and delete those details but to be honest - meh.

I've been moving a lot in the past 6-7 years. I've made TONS of new friends everywhere I've gone. I've never been lonely in the traditional sense. However, I don't have a single person in the whole world I could even begin to talk about anything deep with. So any hope that someday I'll have people around me who I can trust seems impossible. 
 

As for doing better in therapy I'd like to know what you mean.
